parameters.query:
-- Drop existing tables in correct order (dependent tables first)
-- First drop any dependent tables that reference company_data
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS due_diligence_reports CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS complete_dd_reports CASCADE;
-- Now we can safely drop the parent table
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS company_data CASCADE;

-- Create the parent table first
CREATE TABLE company_data (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    company_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    folder_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    content TEXT NOT NULL,
    processed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Create the main due diligence reports table with proper structure
CREATE TABLE due_diligence_reports (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    company_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    introduction_engagement_context TEXT,
    methodology_reliability_levels TEXT,
    company_overview TEXT,
    business_model_unit_economics TEXT,
    products_technology TEXT,
    target_market_competitive_set TEXT,
    financials_multi_year TEXT,
    cash_burn_runway TEXT,
    revenue_quality_client_cohorts TEXT,
    partnerships_ecosystem TEXT,
    intellectual_property TEXT,
    legal_regulatory TEXT,
    governance_board_effectiveness TEXT,
    capital_structure_dilution TEXT,
    risk_matrix_mitigations TEXT,
    gaps_uncertainties_disclaimers TEXT,
    scenario_analysis TEXT,
    strategic_options TEXT,
    recommendations_next_steps TEXT,
    source_map_integrity_log TEXT,
    comprehensive_report_url TEXT,
    status VARCHAR(100),
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    FOREIGN KEY (company_id) REFERENCES company_data(company_id)
);

-- Also create the complete_dd_reports table that other workflows expect
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS complete_dd_reports (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    company_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    
    -- Section content columns that match orchestrator expectations
    introduction_engagement_context TEXT,
    legal_disclaimers_reliance_limitations TEXT,
    methodology_source_validation TEXT,
    financial_trajectory_revenue_quality TEXT,
    partnerships_ecosystem_alliances TEXT,
    intellectual_property_technology TEXT,
    governance_disclosures_risks TEXT,
    appendix_management_rfi TEXT,
    
    -- Legacy columns for backward compatibility
    executive_summary TEXT,
    section3_content TEXT,
    section4_content TEXT,
    section5_content TEXT,
    section6_content TEXT,
    section7_content TEXT,
    section8_content TEXT,
    
    -- Metadata
    sections_completed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'pending',
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    
    FOREIGN KEY (company_id) REFERENCES company_data(company_id)
);

Evidence-based analysis from source documents 📋 REQUIRED HTML STRUCTURE:

1.1 Engagement Summary

Action Labs was engaged by [CLIENT NAME - extract from context] to conduct comprehensive commercial due diligence on [FULL LEGAL COMPANY NAME from source] ([TICKER if public]) for the purpose of evaluating commercial value realization and deal viability. This engagement focuses on assessing the target's commercial scalability, defensibility, and execution friction within the context of potential acquisition or strategic investment.

1.2 Strategic Framing & Evaluative Lens

Our work applies a commercially focused evaluative lens to assess [COMPANY NAME]'s ability to scale, defend market position, and sustain revenue quality over time, under publicly visible constraints. The analysis tests structural revenue sustainability, competitive moats, operational execution capabilities, and market positioning strength. This commercial risk validation examines the target's capacity to deliver consistent returns and maintain strategic advantages in evolving market conditions.

1.3 Scope of Review

This assessment encompasses the following domains, each addressed in dedicated sections with public source citations and reliability ratings:

  • Company structure and organizational architecture
  • Product model and technology positioning
  • Go-to-market strategy and execution
  • Market position and competitive dynamics
  • Revenue structure and customer behavior
  • Financial trajectory and capital efficiency
  • Intellectual property and ecosystem positioning
  • Regulatory exposure and compliance posture
  • Risk pathing and mitigation frameworks

1.4 Data Cutoff & Limitations

This analysis is based exclusively on publicly available information without management access, with data current as of [EXTRACT LATEST FILING DATE from source]. All forward-looking interpretations regarding churn risk, margin structure, and strategic roadmap are evaluated solely to the extent permitted by public documentation. Items requiring management validation are catalogued in Appendix A: Management Interview Script and Appendix B: Diligence RFI Template.

1.5 Authorship & Independence

This report was independently produced by Action Labs without external edits or validations beyond those contained in the sourced regulatory filings and public disclosures. The analysis maintains objectivity through source-verified methodologies and evidence-based conclusions.

1.6 Commercial Orientation Statement

This document is structured to support deal evaluation, negotiation strategy, and next-phase validation planning. Its purpose is to equip [CLIENT NAME] with a decision-useful view of [COMPANY NAME]'s commercial posture, value drivers, and friction points — as derived from the public record. The report emphasizes commercial logic over static profiling, focusing on scalability, defensibility, and execution risk factors critical to investment decision-making.

SOURCE DOCUMENT CONTENT: {{ $json.content }} 🚨 EXECUTION INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Extract REAL company name, ticker, filing dates from source content 2. Replace ALL bracketed placeholders with actual extracted data 3. Use the HTML structure exactly as shown above 4. Write in board-grade, formal commercial tone 5. Focus on strategic commercial evaluation, not generic company description 6. Base ALL statements on evidence from source documents 7. NO fictional data, NO generic examples, NO placeholder text

=You are a senior quality assurance analyst performing final validation on Section 1 content.

{{ $json.generated_content }}

📊 VALIDATION CRITERIA:

- PASS: If content is professional and usable (even if not perfect)

If FAIL, be specific about critical issues that must be fixed.

=You are a senior business analyst performing final approval validation.

📋 SECTION 1 CONTENT FOR FINAL APPROVAL:
{{ $json.generated_content }}

✅ CONTENT ALREADY PASSED INITIAL CHECKER

🎯 FINAL APPROVAL CRITERIA:

CHECKER PROVIDED: {{ $json.checker_feedback }}

- APPROVE: For professional, usable content (recommended approach)
- REJECT: Only for critical defects that prevent report use

If APPROVE, briefly confirm content readiness.
If REJECT, be very specific about critical issues requiring immediate fix.

=You are a senior financial analyst creating a professional due diligence report. {{ $json.retry_attempt ? 'REVISION REQUIRED - Previous content failed quality control.' : 'Generate a comprehensive' }} "Methodology & Reliability Levels" section for: {{ $json.company_name }}

parameters.query:
SELECT 
  company_id,
  company_name,
  introduction_engagement_context,
  methodology_reliability_levels,
  company_overview,
  business_model_unit_economics,
  products_technology,
  target_market_competitive_set,
  financials_multi_year,
  cash_burn_runway,
  revenue_quality_client_cohorts,
  partnerships_ecosystem,
  intellectual_property,
  legal_regulatory,
  governance_board_effectiveness,
  capital_structure_dilution,
  risk_matrix_mitigations,
  gaps_uncertainties_disclaimers,
  scenario_analysis,
  strategic_options,
  recommendations_next_steps,
  source_map_integrity_log,
  status,
  created_at
FROM due_diligence_reports 
WHERE company_id = (SELECT company_id FROM due_diligence_reports ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1)
ORDER BY created_at DESC 
LIMIT 1;
